web_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
book_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
question: Weighing both sides, what should an owner do with the 39.795672 shares after the $150.34 stop breach, and where should capital go?

epigraph.quote: Conviction is not a substitute for a margin of safety.
epigraph.author: Research Desk maxim

web_blocks.html: A balanced verdict starts by steelmanning the bull case for Bloom Energy. Multi-year utility grid queues force data centers and chip fabs toward onsite power [1][18]. Q3 2026 revenue surged 138.1% year over year to $1.236 billion with $225.4 million in GAAP operating income [2][3]. Management lifted FY2026 guidance a third time to $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion [3]. With a 1.2 GW Oracle rollout, a 900 MW NTT DATA deal starting in 2027, a $25 billion Brookfield framework, and Power Connect modules, bulls expect scale leverage toward 2 GW at Fremont [1][20][21][22][23].

The bear case counters that sales growth has outrun cash conversion, contract quality, and balance-sheet discipline. Nine-month CFO minus PP&E was just $41.585 million (1.36% margin) before affiliate investments, while unbilled contract assets reached $858.646 million and inventory hit $927.670 million [2]. Pass 1 found two buyers accounted for 66% of 9M revenue (69% in Q3), with 23% at Brookfield JVs amid 10-Q warnings on neocloud tenant credit [2]. Meanwhile, $5.8 billion in take-or-pay supplier commitments ($2.6 billion in FY2027) dwarf $661.2 million of long-term product RPO [2]. Warranty reserves tripled to $70.267 million, and diluted shares rose 38.0% year over year to 324.289 million [2].

web_blocks.takeaway: Probability-weighted fair value of $76.17 (with Bull equalized at 10.0% WACC) sits 46.5% below the $142.39 close ($142.45 TradingView). Because Base DCF ($75.98) and Base stress cases ($38.13–$53.24) sit far below spot, we reject new capital rather than hedging with WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT.

web_blocks.html: The single hinge claim is whether revenue growth becomes repeatable post-capex free cash flow. That requires collecting $858.6 million in contract assets, absorbing $306.5 million of Oracle contra-revenue warrants, lifting installation margin above -4.8%, and avoiding shortfalls on $5.8 billion of supplier commitments [2][3]. Executive PSUs reward revenue and non-GAAP product margin while ignoring FCF, ROIC, and installation losses across three CFOs in twelve months [47][48][50]. Until cash conversion improves and Stage 4 heals, new capital stays out [55].

web_blocks.html: For current owners, the November 20 close triggers a mandatory stop-loss exit. The ledger holds 39.795672 BE shares: 23.5196 in Schwab ($4,999.96 cost, $3,348.96 value) and 16.276072 in Robinhood ($4,000.00 cost, $2,317.55 value). Total holdings rose from 23.526572 shares on November 12 after Schwab buys logged through November 18. At $142.39, market value is $5,666.51 against $8,999.96 cost, a $3,333.45 loss (-37.04%) and 7.54% of $75,110.60 net worth. Because $142.39 ($142.45 TradingView) closed below our $150.34 prior stop in Stage 4, the action is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 39.795672 shares.

Upward-only stop rules forbid lowering a stop on a losing position to justify holding. Bloom sits in TACTICAL_MOMENTUM with a 4.19 beta, and both trend and valuation fail our gates [55]. Holding for a bounce from 4-hour RSI 27.94 risks deeper capital loss. This call is advisory rather than a live broker order. Verify live quotes, open orders, and tax lots in Schwab and Robinhood before selling.

web_blocks.takeaway: Allocating 100% of BE exit proceeds to cash respects the Downtrend market regime and avoids forcing equity risk. Only ABBV (1.52:1 zone-top R:R) and LLY (2.08:1) meet >=1.50:1 Stage 2 math on Nov 20 snapshots, while AVPT (0.92:1 CMP) and MCK (0.64:1) fail at current snapshot bands.

web_blocks.intro: Because BE is REJECTED (TIER_0) on valuation, negative ex-refund cash conversion, and Stage 4 trend, risk-unit sizing sets 0.0% allocation with no active buy zone or live stop. The $158.76–$163.60 band and $150.34 stop are retired November 12 levels; any conditional valuation watch starts strictly below Base DCF ($75.98) in the $53.24–$68.00 stress-to-discount band ($53.24 equals 12.0% WACC Base DCF).

web_blocks.html: Exit and re-underwrite trigger: sell all 39.795672 held BE shares after the $150.34 stop breach ($142.39 close). Do not reconsider BE for new capital unless price resets below Base DCF ($75.98, into $53.24–$68.00 valuation support) OR Bloom proves repeatable positive post-capex FCF ex-refunds alongside a multi-week Stage 1 base and high-volume reclaim of the 50-day ($234.02) and 200-day ($223.89) SMAs.

Our watch list until the FY2026 Form 10-K (due March 2027) tracks five items [2][3]. Follow Q4 sales conversion against the $1.348B to $1.548B implied target, billing of $858.6M in contract assets, and installation margin recovery [2][3]. Watch warranty cash burn and any shortfall risk on $2.6 billion of FY2027 supplier commitments [2]. Keep the $5,666.51 exit proceeds in cash while the market correction persists [53][57].

book_paragraphs: We now have all the pieces needed to make a clear decision without emotion. Honor the strongest version of the bull thesis first. Bloom solves a real power bottleneck for AI data centers facing multi-year grid delays. Third-quarter revenue jumped 138 percent to $1.236 billion, GAAP operating income hit $225.4 million, and full-year guidance reached $4.5 billion at the midpoint. With Oracle, NTT DATA, Brookfield financing, and Power Connect modules, Bloom has clear commercial momentum.

Now place the bear case beside it. Nine-month operating cash flow minus PP&E was just $41.6 million, or 1.36 percent of sales, before affiliate investments. Unbilled contract assets jumped to $858.6 million and inventory hit $927.7 million. Pass 1 showed customer concentration tightened to 66 percent across two buyers, with 23 percent at Brookfield joint ventures amid 10-Q warnings on neocloud tenant credit. Add $5.8 billion in take-or-pay supplier commitments against $661.2 million of long-term product RPO, tripled warranty reserves, $306.5 million of Oracle warrant offsets, and 38 percent share dilution, and the cash-conversion gap is clear.

Our DCF model quantifies that gap without discount-rate bias. Weighting Bear at $13.50 (40 percent), Base at $75.98 (45 percent), and Bull at $243.88 with an equalized 10 percent WACC (15 percent) yields $76.17 per diluted share. At $142.39, Bloom still trades 87 percent above both Base fair value and expected value. Base downside stresses to $38.13 (6 percent margin), $39.74 (12 percent growth), or $53.24 (12 percent WACC) confirm there is no valuation cushion.

The holding action is equally direct. The ledger holds 39.795672 shares across Schwab (23.5196 shares) and Robinhood (16.276072 shares), worth $5,666.51 against $8,999.96 cost for a $3,333.45 loss and 7.54 percent weight. Closing at $142.39 broke our locked $150.34 prior stop in a Stage 4 breakdown, triggering EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 39.795672 shares. Never widen a stop downward on a tactical loser. Verify live quotes and lots before selling.

Park 100 percent of the $5,666.51 exit proceeds in cash. The S&P 500 is down 11.6 percent from its October peak, QQQ is down over 20 percent, and IWM is in Stage 4. On November 20 snapshots, Stage 2 shortlist leaders AbbVie ($286.20, 1.52:1 zone-top R:R) and Eli Lilly ($1,347.11, 2.08:1 zone-top R:R) clear 1.50:1 asymmetry, whereas AvePoint ($16.49, 0.92:1 at CMP) and McKesson ($1,069.72, 0.64:1 at snapshot zone) fall short at current bands and Cheniere ($294.84) carries $24.138 billion gross debt without a fresh target. Outside peers Cummins ($403.61), GE Vernova ($699.33), and Vertiv ($166.24) are all in Stage 4 breakdowns. Cash preserves optionality until both Bloom and the broader tape repair.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good companies can still be bad trades when valuation, cash conversion, and trend break at once. Honor the $150.34 stop, exit the 39.795672 shares, park the cash, and wait for proof before ever buying back.
